cells.tense: The light you steer by reaches people because you finished what you built, and it reaches them clean.
cells.act: see how it works underneath, apart from this instance
cells.ask: Notice what's underneath a moment when being near someone goes well — the shape of how it works, apart from this particular person. Let that reading carry part of what you usually carry by effort alone.
cells.core:
What you carry toward people has been cultivated, and it shows. You light a space not because you reached for it but because something in you finished and stayed lit. Where two people are trying to line up with each other, that's what makes lining up possible — you can feel alongside someone and stay yourself, and neither gets lost in the other. The shine is real, and it's about connection, which is what keeps it from being performance.

What's free to feed it next is seeing the shape of it. Watch where the pattern stands in your connections — who glows around you, and what happens underneath that — so the understanding does some of the work instead of only the effort. The light doesn't need managing. It needs understanding, so that on a hard day you know what's working and can do it on purpose.

cells.tense: The light you promise people has moved forward of this moment, and you're bracing for a version of it that isn't here.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: With the next person you're trying to help, hold off. Sit a minute and find the piece of them that actually matters now. Begin there — not with the five-year hope, just the piece at hand.
cells.core:
You've been projecting light forward — not onto the people beside you, onto a version of them up ahead — and the shine has started dazzling instead of showing. Where two people are trying to line up with each other, you've already got them lined up somewhere better, and they can feel the distance between where they stand and where you're pointing. It comes from care. It also leaves them behind in the present, where they actually live.

What's back is knowing what to attend to. The next time you're beside someone who's struggling, don't rush the vision. Sit with what you don't know about them yet. Something will land — a small true thing — and that's where you start. Not the whole arc. The next inch. The light comes back into the moment when you stop pointing it at the distance.
cells.sheetLine: You're lighting a version of them that isn't here yet.

cells.tense: The light you steer by stopped reaching anyone, and you still stand where it used to shine.
cells.act: protect the young thing from being judged early
cells.ask: Pick something in you that's still small — a hope, a way with people, a piece of work — and stop holding it next to what it should be. Let it stay young. Tending it plain and daily is the whole of it.
cells.core:
The hope has been waiting so long it stopped arriving. You're still at the door where it used to be, and there's nothing wrong with standing there — except that people stop coming close, and you notice it, and the quiet reads as proof. Whatever you cultivated didn't bloom the way you expected, and you've stopped expecting it to.

What feeds this is care that doesn't exhaust. There's one thing in you that's still young — a hope, a way with people, a piece of work — and it's been judged too early, by you. For a week, tend it without asking progress or a sign or proof. Care for it the way you'd care for something that might still grow. The light doesn't get restored by effort. It gets restored by not being measured before it's ready.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at the door. The light already left it.

cells.tense: You're radiating toward the people around you without knowing it's yours to name.
cells.act: keep it at its real size when you are asked to shrink it
cells.ask: When someone asks what keeps you close to people — or what you bring to a gathering — don't shrink it. Say the true thing, even one sentence. Just don't leave it out when they ask.
cells.core:
There's a warmth you bring to a gathering that people can feel, and when they mention it you hand it off — to the team, to the moment, to just being around. The light has a source. It's yours, and your account of it doesn't include you. Where two people are trying to line up with each other, what makes the lining up work is something you're doing, and you'd tell anyone it's nothing special.

Hold the plain truth of it at size. Not a brag, not a new story about yourself — just when someone asks, don't make it smaller. Hold it the way you'd hold any real thing under pressure: without tightening around it, without letting it be shrunk. Say you're good with people and mean it. That's the whole act. The acknowledgment isn't added to the light. It's what lets it be yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're warm in a gathering. Your word for that is nothing special.

Sentence that serves the writer more than them: 'the way you hold their light is the shape your own...' — cut, it was admiring the mechanism. Verb stays about a star; place stays about connection.
